name: canvas-agent
description: The canvas's tools for kou agents on a canvas: see the board, create and wire nodes, send them work and read what they answer. Only agents on a canvas have it. Generated from kou-canvas's tools: go generate ./cmd/internal/canvascli.

tools.name: CanvasView
tools.description: Show the canvas you are on: every node (its ID, kind, title, status, place and size, ports, worktree), every connection between them, and free places beside your node. Look before you create, connect or remove anything: the canvas changes while you work. To message a node you know the title of, CanvasSend needs no look first.

detail.description: full adds the connections' templates and the notes' texts.

tools.name: CanvasSpawn
tools.description: Create a node on the canvas — a terminal running a coding agent or a command, a kou agent, a note — beside your node unless you say where; optionally wire it to other nodes and give it its first prompt. Give each coding agent that writes code a worktree of its own. It answers the node's ID and place.

preset.description: What the node runs: shell, command (runs command), claude-code, codex, opencode, agent (a kou agent like you), note, or a plugin's preset as plugin/preset.

title.description: Its title, which the other nodes see: short and telling.

command.description: For a command node: the command line it runs.

cwd.description: The directory a terminal starts in, relative to the workspace or to its worktree.

worktree.description: Work in a git worktree of its own, made when missing: its name, its branch kou/<name>. One writer per worktree. A kou agent's worktree is named after its session, whatever the name.

base.description: The branch or commit a new worktree starts from; HEAD by default.

prompt.description: Its first prompt, sent once it runs; for a note, its text.

config.description: More of its configuration, as its preset defines it: model, effort, instructions for an agent; permission_mode for claude-code.

access.description: What its program may do on the canvas: talk by default for what an agent makes; build lets it make nodes too.

near.description: The node to place it beside: yours by default.

side.description: Which side of near: the first free one by default.

x.description: Where it goes, instead of beside near: its left edge.

w.description: Its width; its preset's by default.

h.description: Its height; its preset's by default.

connect.description: Wire it at once: from's output to its input, its output to to's input. A node is its ID or self, with :port when not out or in.

tools.name: CanvasRemove
tools.description: Remove a node from the canvas: one you made, or any with admin access. Its program ends; its worktree stays, with its work.

keep_session.description: Keep a kou agent's session in the session list; it is deleted with the node otherwise.

keep_worktree.description: Worktrees are always kept: only the user removes them.

tools.name: CanvasConnect
tools.description: Connect a node's output to another's input: what the first puts out — a command's output, an agent's answer at the end of its turn — goes to the second as a message.

from.description: The output: a node's ID or self, with :port when not out.

to.description: The input: a node's ID or self, with :port when not in.

template.description: What the message says: {{text}}, {{title}}, {{data.<path>}}, {{from.title}}, {{from.id}}; the output's text by default.

mode.description: approve holds each message until the user lets it go; a connection that closes a loop of agents starts so.

deliver.description: queue (the default) waits until the target is idle; now gives it at once.

tools.name: CanvasDisconnect
tools.description: Remove a connection: by its ID, or by the output and input it joins.

from.description: Or the output it leaves: node or node:port.

to.description: And the input it reaches: node or node:port.

tools.name: CanvasMove
tools.description: Move or resize a node, to keep the canvas tidy.

tools.name: CanvasSend
tools.description: Message a node — a prompt for an agent, a command for a shell — named by its ID or its title: one call, no need to look it up first. With wait, the call waits for the node's answer and returns it: an agent's answer at the end of its turn, a shell's command output. Without wait, an agent's answer comes to you later as a prompt that starts with [canvas] reply from. The text goes in once the node is idle, and Enter is pressed after it; keys are pressed as tmux send-keys names them.

node.description: The node: its ID (n_…) or its title.

text.description: The message: the prompt, or what to type.

wait.description: Wait for the node's answer to this message, and return it. A node that waits for your answer cannot be waited for in turn.

timeout_s.description: With wait: how long to wait at most, in seconds; 600 by default. An answer that comes later comes to you as a reply.

submit.description: Press Enter after the text: true by default.

keys.description: Keys to press after the text, as tmux names them: Enter, Tab, Escape, BSpace, Up, Down, Left, Right, Home, End, C-c, M-x, F1…

when.description: idle (the default) waits until the node is idle; now gives it at once: an agent at work reads it after its current step.

tools.name: CanvasRead
tools.description: Read a node: a terminal's latest lines or screen, the latest output of a node (a command's output, an agent's answer). With wait, wait first — until it is idle, gives its next output, or ends — instead of polling. To ask a node something and have its answer, CanvasSend with wait does it in one call.

node.description: The node: its ID (n_…), its title, or self.

what.description: tail (the default): a terminal's latest lines; screen: what it shows; output or answer: its latest output.

lines.description: How many lines of tail: 80 by default.

wait.description: Wait until the node is idle, gives its next output, or ends, then read.

after.description: With wait output: the count of outputs CanvasSend answered, so that an output given meanwhile counts.

timeout_s.description: How long to wait at most, in seconds: 600 by default.

tools.name: CanvasEmit
tools.description: Put something out of your node now, as its output: it goes along your edges to the nodes your output is connected to. No need to for your answer to a node's message: the answer you end that turn with goes back to it, and along your edges, by itself. What you answer the user stays with the user, unless you emit it.

title.description: A title for it, which templates read as {{title}}.

data.description: Structured data besides the text, which templates read as {{data.<path>}}.
